title: Adapter workflow compact guide and handoff journal
content:
Purpose:
Lightweight, copyable guide for contributors (internal + contractors) to add or update an SDK adapter (client-side integration). Goal: reduce back-and-forth, shorten first-merge time from days to hours.

Target reader:
- New SDK contributor (familiar with JS/TS or Python)
- Solutions engineers pairing with customers on quick integrations

High-level workflow (1-line):
1) Grab template adapter -> 2) run local smoke harness -> 3) implement API surface + telemetry hooks -> 4) run pairing lab -> 5) handoff with artifacts.

Compact onboarding checklist (smoke-test-first):
- [ ] Fork sdk-adapters repo and create feature branch. TODO: standard branch name pattern? (ask git-team)
- [ ] Run 'make dev-adapter' (local dockerized shim). If fails, capture logs and paste to #dev-adopter Slack thread.
- [ ] Confirm basic calls: auth -> model-list -> simple-gen -> embeddings. Use the smoke script at tools/local-smoke/run.sh.
- [ ] Add minimal telemetry: request_id, model_version, latency_ms. Follow telemetry contract: CONFLUENCE-1234.
- [ ] Add unit tests that mock Redwood API (jest/pytest fixtures available under tests/fixtures).
- [ ] Open PR with description template (see PR checklist in repo). Link the Confluence design note if behavior differs from template.

Pairing lab (30–90 min) blueprint:
- Purpose: validate end-to-end behavior with a partner and remove unstated assumptions.
- Pre-req: contributor + reviewer both have project tokens and local dev environment.
- Steps:
  1) 0–5m: walk through feature intent and constraints (latency budget, api contract)
  2) 5–25m: run smoke harness together, reproduce a failing case if present
  3) 25–55m: iterate on edge cases (rate-limit handling, streaming fallback)
  4) 55–75m: add or verify telemetry + logs live in local tracing view
  5) 75–90m: final checklist + record short Loom (2–4 min) showing the flow
- Outcomes to capture in PR: test run screenshot, loom link, reviewer notes.

Handoff artifacts (what to include when handing to QA/SE/Docs):
- Short description (2–3 bullets) of what changed and why.
- Minimal demo script with exact HTTP body examples and expected responses.
- Test vectors (prompt inputs for regression) saved in /tests/test_vectors/<pr-number>.json
- Telemetry map: what new events/fields were added (one-line table).
- Known limitations and mitigation (if streaming not supported, provide fallback).

Common failure modes and quick mitigations:
- Auth mismatch locally: ensure env var RW_API_KEY and RW_ENV set; if using sessions, run tools/auth/refresh.sh.
- Flaky streaming in CI: increase buffer size to 8k and add retry with exponential backoff (0.2s base).
- Test flakes due to model catalog change: pin model id in test fixtures to model-x.y.z.

Notes to self / open questions:
- How strict should adapter template be about batching behavior? (tight coupling -> simpler code vs flexible -> more room for regressions).
- Should we autogenerate telemetry schemas from proto defs? saves time but adds infra work (ticket JIRA-4139).
- Investigate a small helper CLI that scaffolds the PR with templates + test vectors.

Next short-term steps (owner: Alex):
- Prototype a tiny `rbx scaffold-adapter` that'll create branch, template files, and example tests. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Schedule two pairing labs this sprint with SE team. Add sessions to calendar and invite Mina + Daniel.

Appendix (short snippets):
- Local smoke command examples:
  - JS: RW_API_KEY=xxx node examples/basic-gen.js --model gpt-redwood-4 --prompt 'hello'
  - Py: export RW_API_KEY=xxx && python examples/basic_gen.py --model gpt-redwood-4 --prompt 'hello'

- Quick PR template checklist to paste into description:
  - Summary of change (1–2 sentences)
  - Smoke steps + expected results
  - Tests added and how to run them locally
  - Telemetry fields added
  - Reviewer(s) suggested

Rough TODOs (short):
- Move the smoke harness to a single binary script (reduce onboarding friction)
- Finalize branch naming convention and add to repo README
- Draft the small scaffold CLI (prototype)

End of doc.
(Informal notes, intended to be iterated in drive — not canonical until marked final.)
